top_categories.workout_context: 203 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
At Korea Epic Ride, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
26,260ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
129ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Korea Epic Ride's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 203 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
203 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 26,260ft of climbing on mixed mountain/forest — mostly unpaved on the does to your power file on race day.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Korea Epic Ride. Train it until it feels boring.

Road-specific control matters at Korea Epic Ride. Practice on mixed mountain/forest — mostly unpaved on the: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 203 miles.
Low-cadence force work supports 26,260ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
26,260ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.

race_overlay.weather: June in Songjeon Beach, Sonyang-myeon, Yangyang-gun, Gangwon-do, South Korea — Early June in Gangwon-do's mountains and East Sea coast: variable mountain weather with real rain risk, and forest roads vulnerable to washout. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, including rain protection and wet-road braking before Korea Epic Ride. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 203 miles: 80–100g carbs/hour from mile 1 — don’t wait until you’re hungry. Practice your exact race-day nutrition in every long training ride. Carry backup calories. 203 miles burns 8,000–12,000+ calories — you cannot replace them all, but you must try.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Korea Epic Ride. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Over Under, and Mixed Climbing to prepare you for 203 miles of mixed mountain/forest — mostly unpaved on the offroad routes in Songjeon Beach, Sonyang-myeon, Yangyang-gun, Gangwon-do, South Korea.
